clue.text: What's needed for one being sick on street?

definitions.text: What's needed for one being sick on street?

indicators.note: in a down-or-across charade, one piece written on another follows it; here the sick person comes after the street

parts.note: someone vomiting is a retcher

explanation.surface: A riddle about what you would need if someone threw up in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, while 'on' puts the retching person after ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is the litter used to carry an ill or injured person, which is exactly what someone taken sick in the road needs.

clue.text: Greek character drops temperature in part of plant

indicators.note: the plant part drops, i.e. loses, the letter

parts.note: the stigma is the part of a flower's pistil that receives pollen

explanation.surface: A Greek figure lets the temperature fall in a section of the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a Greek character.

clue.text: Going through book, girl admits love to be theme of ballad

parts.note: reading is going through a book

indicators.note: the girl's word lets in, or admits, the letter

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
O is love, nil in tennis

explanation.surface: While reading, a girl confesses her love, which becomes the subject of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde's poem is The Ballad of Reading Gaol, Reading being an English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's The Ballad of Reading Gaol takes the prison where he was held as its subject.

clue.text: Opera, like, heartless? That's relatively accurate

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera

indicators.note: the inner letters of the word are cut out, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: Is an opera somehow lacking feeling? A fairly accurate verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' cuts IK from LIKE, leaving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A model built to scale has every part correct in proportion to the others, so it is accurate relatively.

clue.text: Line of trees chap would propagate round either side of estate

parts.note: he'd is short for he would

indicators.note: the contraction and verb go round, i.e. surround, the letter

parts.note: to grow plants is to propagate them
the word estate begins and ends with E, so either side gives that letter

explanation.surface: A man would plant a row of trees along both edges of his land.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedgerow is a line of shrubs and trees bordering a field.

clue.text: Put record in to storage container and tidy cases

indicators.note: the record is put in to, i.e. into, the rack

parts.note: a rack holds and stores things
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Instructions to file a record in its case and tidy up the luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is a link: the record goes into the rack.
explanation.definitionFit: To repack is to pack again, so tidying suitcases by rearranging their contents.

clue.text: Tree seen in mist at length

parts.note: haze is a light mist

explanation.surface: A tree glimpsed through mist from a long way off.
explanation.definitionFit: The hazel is a small nut-bearing tree, so it is an example of a tree.

clue.text: Writers' village has endless value

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: worth is value

explanation.surface: A literary village is said to be worth a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: HAWORTH is the Yorkshire village where the Brontë sisters lived and wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: Haworth is famous as the home of the Brontë sisters, a village of writers.

clue.text: Spot instrument woman's dropped

indicators.note: the instrument has the woman's word taken off its end

parts.note: a zither is a stringed instrument
her is the word for a woman, and the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A woman has dropped her musical instrument on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Zit is slang for a pimple, i.e. a spot on the skin.

clue.text: Opera is long, with her in cast

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould, so the letters are thrown into a new form

explanation.surface: An opera runs long, and she is in the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges LONG and HER into LOHENGR, with IN kept after; 'cast' looks like the opera's cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lohengrin is Wagner's opera about the swan knight.

clue.text: Girl is after good measure of wine

indicators.note: the girl comes after the good, so her word follows the single letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman wants a decent serving of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is served and measured by the glassful, so a glass is a measure of wine.

clue.text: Departs East Anglian town — about time, having control of car

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

indicators.note: the town's name goes about, i.e. around, the letter for time

parts.note: Ipswich is the county town of Suffolk in East Anglia

explanation.surface: A train schedule: leaving an East Anglian town at last, with someone at the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: IPSWICH is a town in Suffolk, eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip switch is the dashboard switch that dips a car's headlights, one of the driver's controls.

clue.text: Film no actor could make?

parts.note: a film in which no live performer appears, every character being drawn and brought to life frame by frame

explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon film is made from drawings, so no actor appears on screen in it.

clue.text: Glass to repack here? Time to work

definitions.meaning: glass and repack are the answers at 9 and 5 in this grid, so the phrase reads as the working day from nine until five
the hours when a business is open and staff are at their desks

explanation.walkthrough: GLASS is the answer to 9 across and REPACK to 5 down, so 'Glass to repack' is 'nine to five'.
explanation.definitionFit: Office hours are the regular working hours, typically from nine in the morning to five.

clue.text: Very important to keep united? I don't think so, for foreign Protestant

indicators.note: the big word holds, or keeps, the letter inside it

parts.note: something huge is very big or very important
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
a flat refusal or denial, as in 'not likely'

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether it matters to stay united and answers no, of a foreign Protestant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Huguenots were French Calvinist Protestants, many of whom fled abroad, so they are a foreign Protestant group.

clue.text: 9 may stand up

definitions.meaning: a glass, the answer to 9 across, may contain liquid
an argument that stands up is valid under scrutiny

explanation.walkthrough: 9 refers to the answer at 9 across, GLASS, which can contain liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory that holds water is sound and stands up to examination.

clue.text: Irritating beetle?

definitions.meaning: jokingly, something that rubs and irritates the skin is one that chafes
a large beetle, as in cockchafer

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a frivolous coinage: a thing that chafes, i.e. irritates.
explanation.definitionFit: Chafer is a genuine name for a family of large beetles, and playfully also something that chafes.

clue.text: Delivery one turns away

definitions.meaning: a ball bowled in cricket is a delivery
a ball that spins away from the batsman after pitching

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a leg break is a spinning ball that turns from the leg side towards the off, away from a right-handed batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg break is a type of cricket ball bowled with spin that turns away from the batter.

clue.text: Roof needs clean top, but not edges

indicators.note: the outer letters of the phrase are dropped, so the answer sits concealed inside it

explanation.surface: A roof wants its top washed but its gutters left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not edges' strips the C and P from 'clean top', leaving the answer lying inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed or roof propped against a wall, a type of simple roof.

clue.text: Secure sort of house to have

parts.note: a tied house is a British pub bound to sell one brewery's beer
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Making certain of a particular kind of home of one's own.
explanation.walkthrough: A TIED house is a British pub owned by a brewery and obliged to sell its beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie down something is to fasten it firmly, i.e. secure it.

clue.text: Emergency rations in camp: mine need cooking

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are mixed up and reworked

explanation.surface: Survival food in a military camp still needs to be heated up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pemmican is dried meat pressed with fat, a concentrated food carried as emergency rations by explorers.

clue.text: Like girl's mother, one beauty

parts.note: ma is mother
I is the Roman numeral one
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A girl's mother is said to be just as lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidish means resembling a maid, an old word for a girl.

clue.text: A cut closes university hall

indicators.note: the cut word closes around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to trim is to cut

explanation.surface: Funding cuts force a university hall to shut.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is a central hall or open court in a building.

clue.text: Film director ad-libs the moves around set

parts.note: Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane

indicators.note: the letters are moved around, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: A film director improvises while the actors wander about the set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves around' rearranges ADLIBSTHE into TABLISHED. Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane; 'set' looks like a film set but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set, as in set in its ways, is firmly fixed and long established.

clue.text: Old invader grasps top of cannon ball

indicators.note: the invader holds the letter within

parts.note: Danes invaded Britain in Viking times

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is its top in a down clue

explanation.surface: A Viking raider seizes a cannon ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a formal party for dancing, and a dance is such an event.

clue.text: I chuck in uninteresting fossil

indicators.note: the throwing pieces go in the dull word

parts.note: trite means stale and dull
to lob is to chuck or toss

explanation.surface: Someone tosses a boring old fossil away.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilobites are extinct marine arthropods known almost entirely as fossils.

clue.text: Troublemaker every constituency has?

parts.note: each parliamentary seat returns one Member of Parliament, read as the Roman numeral for one plus the letters for that member

explanation.walkthrough: Every UK constituency has one MP (Member of Parliament), written I MP.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a mischievous little devil, a troublemaker.

clue.text: That's posh, a name for Welshman

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, 'that is'
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain name sounds rather upper-class for a Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ieuan is a Welsh form of John, a name borne by Welshmen.

clue.text: Get ready to open state prison

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
pen is slang for a prison, short for penitentiary

explanation.surface: A new state prison prepares for its opening day.
explanation.walkthrough: Some fruits and seed pods burst open once mature, which justifies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or pods mature before splitting, so maturing is getting ready to open.

clue.text: Clever chap parrots note about heroin and speed

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, so a learned person

indicators.note: the birds and the note go about, i.e. around, the drug letter

parts.note: the kea is a New Zealand parrot
H is slang for heroin
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A clever man's parrots pick up a note mentioning heroin and amphetamine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the drug letter inside the birds plus note. 'speed' looks like the drug but is the verb; 'Clever chap' is a holder of a Master of Arts degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To make haste is to hurry, the verb sense of speed.
